Global benchmark Brent has retreated by more than a fifth so far this month, as supplies from the Middle East recovered and Trump held off on renewed large-scale strikes against the Islamic Republic. Still, there’s been a flare-up in low-level fighting across the region in recent days, including a spate of attacks on vessels transiting the critical Strait of Hormuz.
“We are not yet at the point where the narrative of improving supply is enough to overshadow the military flare-ups in the region,” said Florence Schmit, a senior energy strategist at Rabobank. “Flows through Hormuz have improved, yet ships are still being attacked and President Trump is yet again considering plans for another round of extensive strikes on Iran.”
